title: Pandas Examples
description: Small Pandas examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Build a DataFrame
examples.description: A DataFrame is a table with labelled columns and rows. Each list supplied here becomes one column.
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

print(df.shape)

examples.title: Select a column
examples.description: Selecting one column by name returns a Series. A Series is a labelled one-dimensional set of values.
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

print(df["score"].tolist())

examples.title: Read by label with loc
examples.description: loc selects using row and column labels. This table has default row labels 0, 1 and 2.
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

print(df.loc[1, "name"])

examples.title: Read by position with iloc
examples.description: iloc selects by zero-based positions. Its row and column numbers describe where values are placed.
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

print(df.iloc[0, 1])

examples.title: Filter rows
examples.description: A condition creates a true-or-false value for each row. Use that condition to keep matching rows.
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

passed = df[df["score"] >= 8]
print(passed["name"].tolist())

examples.title: Add a calculated column
examples.description: A new column can come from a calculation on an existing one. Matching rows keep their relationship.
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

df["bonus_score"] = df["score"] + 1
print(df["bonus_score"].tolist())

examples.title: Sort rows by a value
examples.description: sort_values orders rows by a selected column. The other columns move with their row so names and scores stay matched.
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

ordered = df.sort_values("score")
print(ordered["name"].tolist())

examples.title: Handle missing values
examples.description: A missing value means data is absent. isna identifies missing entries; filling them requires a justified choice.
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

values = pd.Series([2.0, None, 6.0])
print(values.isna().tolist())

examples.title: Group and summarise
examples.description: groupby gathers rows with the same key. An aggregation, such as mean, gives one summary for each group.
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

means = df.groupby("team")["score"].mean()
print(float(means.loc["red"]))

examples.title: Join related tables
examples.description: merge combines tables using shared keys. Check whether each key is unique before deciding how the join should behave.
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

teams = pd.DataFrame({"team": ["red", "blue"], "room": ["A", "B"]})
joined = df.merge(teams, on="team", validate="many_to_one")
print(joined.loc[joined["name"] == "Ben", "room"].iloc[0])

examples.title: Read a tiny CSV
examples.description: CSV stores rows as text separated by commas. read_csv can read it from a file or, here, an in-memory text buffer.
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

from io import StringIO
small = pd.read_csv(StringIO("item,count\nbook,2\npen,3\n"))
print(small["count"].sum())

examples.title: Copy a selected table before changing it
examples.description: Make your intended copy explicit when you want to edit a subset independently. This keeps the original table easier to reason about.
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

selected = df.loc[df["team"] == "red"].copy()
selected["score"] = 0
print(df["score"].tolist())
